leftColumn.title: Standard Bar Charts
leftColumn.subtitle: Two-Dimensional Grid (Price vs. Time)
bullets: X-axis strictly plots uniform elapsed time
Prints candles even during dead sideways chop
Volume bars track turnover under each period

rightColumn.title: Point & Figure Charts
rightColumn.subtitle: One-Dimensional (Price Alone)
bullets: No time axis whatsoever on the horizontal scale
Column advances only on predetermined price movement
Ignores low-volume churn and random drift completely

beats.hindi_tts: On a Point and Figure chart, X represents rising demand and O denotes falling supply; they never share a column.

leftColumn.title: Column of X's
leftColumn.subtitle: Bulls Dominating Demand

Represents rising prices and buyer aggression
Cannot switch to downward plot in same column

rightColumn.title: Column of O's
rightColumn.subtitle: Bears Dominating Supply
bullets: Plotted downward as price declines box by box
Represents falling prices and seller control
Shifts right only when reversal threshold is cleared

beats.hindi_tts: While bar chart trendlines follow arbitrary angles, P&F trendlines are strictly drawn at 45 degrees.
beats.en_subtitle: While bar chart trendlines follow arbitrary angles, P&F trendlines are strictly drawn at 45 degrees.

leftColumn.title: Bullish Support Line (45° Up)
leftColumn.subtitle: Plotted Up and to the Right from a Major Low
bullets: Starts at lowest O and angles up at exactly 45°
Acts as the definitive institutional bull rail
Long as prices hold above line, trend is firmly bullish

rightColumn.title: Bearish Resistance Line (45° Down)
rightColumn.subtitle: Plotted Down and to the Right from a Major Peak
bullets: Starts at highest X and angles down at exactly 45°
Acts as ceiling overhead during bear campaigns
Long positions are strictly forbidden beneath this line

beats.en_narration: While bar chart trendlines follow arbitrary angles, P&F trendlines are strictly drawn at 45 degrees.

beats.hindi_tts: Because grid boxes are square, a 45-degree line represents the precise mathematical balance of price and column.
beats.en_subtitle: Because grid boxes are square, a 45-degree line represents the precise mathematical balance of price and column.

leftColumn.title: Bullish Support Line (45° Up)
leftColumn.subtitle: Mathematical Precision
bullets: Advances 1 box up for every 1 column across
Complete objectivity: no angle dispute between chartists

rightColumn.title: Bearish Resistance Line (45° Down)
rightColumn.subtitle: Overhead Ceiling
bullets: Declines 1 box down for every 1 column across
Penetration of this line signals a definitive macro trend change

beats.en_narration: Because grid boxes are square, a 45-degree line represents the precise mathematical balance of price and column.

leftColumn.title: The Golden Execution Rule

ui_state.question: On a 3-box reversal chart with a ₹5 box size, a stock is in an ascending column of X's at ₹650. What is the exact price drop required to print an O column, and how many O's will appear at once?
ui_state.answer: Price must drop by at least ₹15 (3 boxes × ₹5) to ₹635. Exactly 3 O's will be plotted simultaneously in the new column to the right (at ₹645, ₹640, and ₹635). Any drop less than ₹15 is completely ignored.
